key_insight: CASE turns a vision-language model from a passive answerer into an agent that actively searches longitudinal patient records and MRI evidence before reasoning.
clinical_relevance: This could improve evidence-grounded medical AI for follow-up assessment, where the key challenge is selecting and comparing the right prior visits, modalities, and regions over time.
method: Built a longitudinal multimodal benchmark from UK Biobank with patient-specific clinical context and baseline/follow-up MRI.
Trained compact vision-language agents using 14,734 frontier-model interaction trajectories for supervised fine-tuning.
Added agentic reinforcement learning plus self-distillation and rubric-based LLM feedback to refine evidence-seeking behavior.
evidence_signal: The benchmark includes 50,401 clinical questions from 4,739 participants, and the Qwen3-VL-8B agent reportedly outperformed GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.8 by over 16% and 10% relative answer accuracy under matched evaluation.
watch_item: Performance was shown in a controlled benchmark environment, so real-world clinical deployment would still need careful validation for robustness, safety, and workflow integration.
paper_title: From Given to Gathered Evidence: Agentic Learning for Longitudinal Medical Reasoning
